{{short description|American college basketball season}} {{Use American English|date=March 2026}} {{Use mdy dates|date=August 2023}} {{Infobox college sports team season | team = Duke Blue Devils | year = 2021–22 | sport = basketball | logo = Duke Blue Devils basketball mark.svg | logo_size = 125 | conference = [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] | short_conf = ACC | CoachRank = 3 | APRank = 9 | record = 32–7 | conf_record = 16–4 | head_coach = [[Mike Krzyzewski]] | hc_year = 42nd | assoc_coach = [[Jon Scheyer]] | asst_coach2 = [[Chris Carrawell]] | asst_coach3 = [[Nolan Smith]] | captain = | stadium = [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] | champion = ACC regular season champions | tourney = [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] | tourney_result = Final Four }} {{2021–22 ACC men's basketball standings}} The '''2021–22 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team''' represented [[Duke University]] during the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. They played their home games at [[Cameron Indoor Stadium]] in [[Durham, North Carolina]], as a member of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]]. On June 2, 2021, the school announced that Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] would retire following the completion of the 2021–22 season after 42 years as head coach of Duke and 47 years of coaching.{{Cite web|date=2021-06-02|title=Coach K retiring in '22; Scheyer named successor|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/31553654/duke-blue-devils-coach-mike-krzyzewski-plans-leave-season-leave-next-season-sources-say|access-date=2021-06-04|website=ESPN.com|language=en}} Associate head coach [[Jon Scheyer]] was named the head coach in waiting, to become the team's new head coach after the conclusion of the season.{{Cite web|last=WRAL|date=2021-06-04|title=Duke introduces Jon Scheyer as next basketball coach|url=https://www.wralsportsfan.com/duke-introduces-jon-scheyer-as-next-basketball-coach/19710570/|access-date=2021-06-04|website=WRALSportsFan.com|language=en}} After losing to [[Carolina–Duke rivalry|longtime rival]] [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]] in their final home game, the team made it to the NCAA Tournament for the first time since [[2019 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2019]], as [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|the 2020 tournament was cancelled]] and Duke did not make the 2021 tournament. Duke reached the Final Four for the 13th time under Krzyzewski, where they again lost to North Carolina 81–77 in their first-ever NCAA tournament meeting. ==Previous season== In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the [[2020–21 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Blue Devils]] finished the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2020–21 season]] 13–11, 9–9 to finish in 10th place in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]]. Their season ended with their withdrawal from the [[ACC tournament]] due to positive COVID-19 tests within the program.{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2021/03/11/duke-positive-coronavirus-test/|title=Duke's season over after positive coronavirus test ends its ACC tournament|newspaper=Washington Post|date=March 11, 2021|accessdate=April 21, 2021}} As a result, the Blue Devils failed to receive a bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] for the first time since [[1994–95 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|1995]], ending the second longest [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament consecutive appearances|active streak of NCAA appearances]].{{cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2021/03/duke-basketball-misses-ncaa-tournament-march-madness-selection-sunday|title=BUBBLE POPPED: Duke men's basketball misses NCAA tournament for first time in 26 years|website=dukechronicle.com|publisher=Duke Chronicle|date=March 14, 2021|accessdate=April 21, 2021}} ==Offseason== ===Coaching changes=== After it became clear that Scheyer would be taking over for Coach K in 2022, associate head coach [[Nate James (basketball)|Nate James]] left the school to become the new head coach at [[Austin Peay Governors basketball|Austin Peay]].{{Cite web|last=Krest|first=Shawn|title=Nate James Named Head Coach at Austin Peay|url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/basketball/nate-james-head-coach-austin-peay|access-date=2021-06-04|website=Sports Illustrated|date=April 2, 2021 |language=en}} [[Nolan Smith]], previously the director of basketball operations, was promoted to assistant coach, joining Jon Scheyer and [[Chris Carrawell]].{{cite web|url=https://www.newsobserver.com/sports/college/acc/duke/article250462281.html#:~:text=Nolan%20Smith%2C%20the%202011%20ACC,assistant%20coach%20on%20Duke's%20staff.|title=Coach K promotes Nolan Smith to assistant coach.
